title: Nonsurgical Management of Horizontal Root Fracture with Necrotic Apical Segment and Coronal Cervical Abfraction using Mineral Trioxide Aggregate: Case Report
html: Horizontal root fractures are relatively rare dental findings and often pose diagnostic and treatment challenges. In addition to a horizontal root fracture, this case report also demonstrates a finding of a noncarious cervical abfraction lesion, which involves the loss of dental hard tissue from the cervical areas of teeth through processes unrelated to caries. A 22 -year-old healthy female patient was complaining of the maxillary left first premolar area with a history of dental trauma. Clinically, the tooth presented with a noncarious cervical abfraction lesion.
